paper-unveiling-protein-corona-compositi.summary: This paper predicts the composition of the protein corona formed on nanoparticle surfaces using resampling-based data balancing (Random Oversampling, SmoteR, WERCS) combined with machine learning models, notably Random Forest, to address imbalanced abundance data. It validates predictions against label-free quantification data for four nanoparticle types. CTGAN is cited only in the reference list alongside other tabular-data ML methods, with no evidence it was implemented or run.

paper-validation-machine-learning-ids-20.summary: This paper proposes an end-to-end machine-learning intrusion detection system (IDS) design framework for SCADA-based power systems, covering dataset preprocessing, data augmentation, automated feature selection, and rigorous cross-validation/testing, validated on the public ORNL power-system SCADA dataset. Random Forest trained on an augmented, class-balanced dataset achieved the best F1 score (94.09%) against unseen data. CT-GAN, the CTGAN tabular synthesizer from the SDV family, is run directly to generate synthetic normal-traffic records that balance the training set, making it the generator underlying the paper's central augmentation and IDS-performance results.
paper-validation-machine-learning-ids-20.needs: Evidence does not show an explicit import statement or SDV library name for the CT-GAN run (vs. the separately mentioned SDV/YData platforms), so whether the standalone ctgan package or sdv.tabular API was invoked is not fully certain.

paper-driven-framework-inter-frequency-2.summary: This paper proposes TORIS, a data-driven framework for predicting and mitigating inter-frequency handover failures in 5G networks, combining a novel feature set from drive-test data with multiple data-augmentation techniques to address class imbalance and a transmit-power tuning heuristic. To generate synthetic minority-class handover data, the authors run conditional tabular GAN (CTGAN), tuning and grid-searching hyperparameters (Table II lists CTGAN hyperparameters) and comparing its performance against a Chow-Liu Bayesian Network approach and borderline-SMOTE. SDV's CTGAN is run as one of several data-augmentation generators for the handover-failure prediction task, while the original SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) paper is cited as the source of the CLBN algorithm they implement for CLBN-based data generation.
paper-driven-framework-inter-frequency-2.needs: The SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) paper [35] is cited for a CLBN algorithm the authors say they 'utilized'; unclear whether this reimplements the algorithm from scratch (port) or invokes SDV's CLBN synthesizer directly, so its integration mode is uncertain even though CTGAN's api_user use is well evidenced.

paper-autoscore-imbalance-interpretable-.summary: This paper presents AutoScore-Imbalance, an extension of the AutoScore clinical-score-generation framework designed to handle rare-event, class-imbalanced electronic health record data through training-set optimization, sample-weight optimization, and an adjusted scoring model, validated on ICU mortality prediction using MIMIC-derived data. The full text obtained shows no passage discussing CTGAN, its architecture, or its use as a data-augmentation method, despite OpenAlex metadata listing the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper among its citations. CTGAN is therefore treated here only as a bibliographic citation whose actual engagement in the body text could not be located in the extracted evidence.
paper-autoscore-imbalance-interpretable-.needs: Full text extraction found no SDV/CTGAN mention despite metadata citation; unclear whether CTGAN was used as an oversampling baseline or only cited in a reference the extraction missed. Cannot verify actual usage or engagement from available evidence.

paper-explainable-machine-learning-solut.summary: This paper proposes an explainable AI pipeline that infers the likely histopathological outcome for thoracic cancer patients and estimates the optimal timing for surgical intervention, combining a deep neural classifier with stabilized LIME explanations trained on manually labeled clinical data. It reports a 7% improvement over surgeon opinion alone on a case study, with reproducibility details for both medical and technical aspects. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni) is cited only in the reference list, with no engagement in the body text.

paper-fbipt-robust-reversible-database-2.summary: This paper proposes FBIPT, a reversible relational-database watermarking scheme that embeds ownership information via inserted 'position tuples' computed from Group, Feature, and Control Fields rather than modifying the source data directly, and shows it is more robust than prior watermarking methods on numerical and non-numerical attributes alike. The scheme is generator-agnostic: any synthetic data generator can supply the inserted position tuples. CTGAN is cited as an example of an existing high-performing synthetic data generator that could be used to construct such tuples quickly, but it is not implemented or evaluated in the reported experiments.
paper-fbipt-robust-reversible-database-2.needs: No experimental section confirms CTGAN was actually implemented; it is cited only as an example of a fast synthetic data generator applicable to FBIPT.

paper-mixed-imputation-generative-advers.summary: This paper proposes a missing-data imputation approach for mixed (numerical and categorical) datasets that first oversamples the observed training data using tabular GAN variants before training MissForest, MICE, and denoising autoencoder imputers, showing that added synthetic samples improve imputation accuracy especially at high missingness ratios. It evaluates four UCI datasets across multiple train/test splits and missingness ratios. TGAN and CTGAN are run as the two generators producing the synthetic oversampled training data that the whole empirical evaluation rests on.
paper-mixed-imputation-generative-advers.needs: No package name, import statement, or CTGAN constructor hyperparameters appear in the visible text, so it is unclear whether the sdv-dev CTGAN/TGAN packages were run directly (api_user) or reimplemented by the authors (port); descriptions of PacGAN-based conditional generator and GMM mode normalization could be either quoting the original papers or describing their own build.

paper-automated-imbalanced-learning-deep.summary: This paper proposes AutoSMOTE, a hierarchical reinforcement-learning framework that jointly decides how many and where to place synthetic minority-class samples for imbalanced classification, formulating the SMOTE generation process as a multi-level MDP optimized directly on the validation performance metric. It is evaluated against 85 SMOTE variants, meta-learning methods, and generative baselines on six real-world datasets. CTGAN (and TVAE) from the sdv-dev/CTGAN repository is run with default hyperparameters as one of several over-sampling baselines compared against AutoSMOTE.

paper-videotrain-gan-adaptive-framework-.summary: This paper presents VideoTrain++, a GAN-based adaptive framework for generating synthetic network traffic traces representing video streaming sessions, aimed at supporting network research and testing without requiring real video content. The framework is evaluated for its ability to reproduce realistic traffic patterns for downstream network simulation or analysis tasks. It cites the SDV-family vine copula paper, apparently as related prior work on synthetic data generation methods, though no details of any actual use are available.
paper-videotrain-gan-adaptive-framework-.needs: Full text and citing sentence needed to confirm whether vine copula methods were actually used or merely cited as background.

paper-generating-synthetic-fermentation-.summary: This paper proposes a pipeline combining multiple imputation ensemble (MICE and random-forest imputation, bagged and stacked) with a custom-remodeled tabular GAN, incorporating skip connections and a Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty, to generate synthetic fermentation data for Shindari, a traditional Jeju beverage, for downstream prediction and microbial spoilage control. The authors describe their own generator's handling of continuous variables (value scalar plus cluster vector) and categorical variables (probability distribution) in prose, citing Xu & Veeramachaneni's tabular GAN paper as the source of this design idea rather than running its code. TGAN's mode-specific value/cluster representation for continuous columns is cited only as prior art informing the authors' own reimplemented architecture, with no SDV-family library executed.
paper-generating-synthetic-fermentation-.needs: Confirm whether the cited technique (value scalar + cluster vector) is being mis-attributed to TGAN rather than CTGAN, since mode-specific normalization is more commonly associated with the latter.

paper-identifying-mobile-sensing-indicat.summary: This paper builds a passive-sensing and EMA-based system to identify and predict indicators of psychological resilience among medical resident physicians, using wearable and smartphone data collected during a high-stress internship year. The authors design custom conditional GAN-style density estimation models, based on encoder-decoder neural network architectures, to model shifts between baseline and internship feature distributions. In describing how they modeled mood as a continuous variable, they cite the TGAN paper (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) for its approach to handling continuous variables, adopting the idea in their own custom generative model rather than running the TGAN/SDV library itself.
paper-identifying-mobile-sensing-indicat.needs: Unclear whether the TGAN continuous-variable technique was directly reimplemented or merely referenced conceptually; no library import or run is evidenced.

paper-reducing-misclassifications-error-.summary: This paper proposes RtoSynR, a real-to-synthetic-real data augmentation scheme that generates synthetic transaction records from a sample of real data to enlarge the training set for CART-based debit card fraud classifiers, aiming to reduce class imbalance and misclassification. The authors report improved classification accuracy for CART models trained on the augmented RtoSynR dataset compared to models trained on real data alone. SDV (cited as Neha et al. 2016, 'The Synthetic Data Vault') is referenced only in passing to support the claim that synthesized data can match real data in downstream accuracy, with no SDV code or method used.
paper-reducing-misclassifications-error-.needs: The whole text was searched and no SDV-family term appears outside the reference list beyond this single cited finding; SDV is not run or engaged with methodologically.

preprint-close-reality-interpretable-fea.summary: This preprint introduces DPG-da, a data-augmentation framework that extracts interpretable decision predicates from trained models to enforce domain constraints during over-sampling, aiming to produce diverse yet feasible and interpretable synthetic minority-class samples. The method is benchmarked against a large set of over-sampling techniques including SMOTE variants, ROS, and generative tabular models across many real-world imbalanced datasets, measuring F1-score and runtime. CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN (from the SDV library) are run unmodified as three of twelve baseline over-sampling methods compared against DPG-da.

preprint-synthesizing-real-world-distrib.summary: This paper proposes DiMSO (Distribution Mapping with Shuffled Optimization), a fully-connected neural network that maps high-dimensional Gaussian noise to a target tabular distribution, combined with PCA for privacy and two novel Wasserstein/covariance-based loss functions. It is evaluated against traditional and deep-learning generators (SMOTE, Synthpop, TabDiff, CTGAN, TVAE) across 25 tabular datasets on distributional similarity, privacy, and downstream classification utility. CTGAN and TVAE, drawn from the synthetic data vault library, are run as deep-learning baseline generators throughout the comparison, and Gaussian Copula from the same library is discussed as a traditional statistical alternative.

preprint-semantic-training-gap-ontology-.summary: This paper identifies a 'semantic training gap' in LLM-based industrial AI agents deployed for manufacturing analytics, where agents lack grounded understanding of the relational structure linking equipment identifiers, process parameters, and regulatory constraints. It proposes an ontology-grounded tool architecture with a three-operation interface contract that reduces tool-parameter hallucination from 43% to 0% in controlled experiments, validated via a digital twin platform. SDV is only cited in passing among statistical data generators noted to lack causal coherence, not run or engaged with further.

paper-synthetic-tabular-survey-2025.summary: Surveys synthetic tabular data generation under a three-fold taxonomy of traditional machine learning methods, diffusion models and large language model approaches, comparing them on data type compatibility, fidelity, privacy resilience and downstream performance, and cataloguing the datasets and metrics the field uses. CTGAN is one of the surveyed methods rather than a tool the survey runs: it heads the conditional GAN branch of the taxonomy with TVAE under the VAE branch, and the prose credits it with the PacGAN discriminator, a combined generator and gradient-penalty Wasserstein loss, and training-by-sampling for imbalanced categorical features.

preprint-causal-analysis-social-support-.summary: This medRxiv preprint applies causal inference methods (propensity scores, TMLE) to a synthetic stroke rehabilitation dataset to test whether high social support causally affects functional outcomes 12 months post-stroke, finding no significant effect once depression is adjusted for as a confounder. The synthetic dataset underlying the entire analysis was generated using SDV's Gaussian Copula Synthesizer and assessed with SDV's evaluation framework, achieving a 95.75% overall quality score. SDV's GaussianCopula synthesizer is run as the generator producing the synthetic data the whole causal analysis rests on, with its quality report used to validate fidelity.

preprint-graph-conditional-flow-matching.summary: This paper proposes a generative model for multi-table relational data that uses flow matching with a graph neural network denoiser to model the content of an entire relational database conditioned on its foreign-key graph structure. The method is evaluated against several relational synthesis baselines (SDV, ClavaDDPM, RCTGAN, REaLTabFormer) on benchmark datasets including AirBnB, Rossmann, Walmart, CORA, IMDB MovieLens, and Biodegradability, using an XGBoost-based discriminator fidelity metric. SDV's Hierarchical Modeling Algorithm is described as the pioneering multi-table Gaussian-copula synthesizer and is run as one of the comparison baselines, notably failing to scale to the IMDB dataset.
preprint-graph-conditional-flow-matching.needs: Citations tagged 'tgan-2018' in the evidence largely refer to Xu et al. 2018's Graph Isomorphism Network paper, not Xu & Veeramachaneni's TGAN -- likely a citation-matching artifact rather than genuine TGAN engagement.

paper-imbllm-oversampling-2025.summary: Oversamples the minority class by prompting a fine-tuned language model and then interpolating between generated and majority records, arguing that the diversity of the added samples matters more than their proximity to the real minority, and reports the best or second-best classifier accuracy on eight of ten datasets. CTGAN and TVAE are the two generative baselines among eight oversamplers, run from the sdv-dev implementation, with CTGAN the strongest competitor throughout the comparison.

preprint-empirical-privacy-evaluations-g.summary: This paper is a review of empirical privacy evaluation methods for machine learning-based generative and predictive models, focused on the practical challenges of assessing privacy risk for synthetic data used with large datasets such as those from statistical agencies and healthcare providers. It surveys threat models and attack techniques (e.g., nearest-record distance, membership inference) and identifies a trade-off between computational feasibility and realism of the assumed adversary. TGAN (Xu and Veeramachaneni, 2018) is cited only in passing as one of several prior works that evaluate privacy via distance to the nearest synthetic record.

preprint-generating-tabular-heterogeneou.summary: This paper proposes Heterogeneous Sequential Feature Forest Flow (HS3F), a feature-by-feature tabular data generator that combines conditional flow matching with XGBoost, improving on the earlier Forest Flow method by handling categorical variables via multinomial sampling and using a Runge-Kutta ODE solver for faster, higher-quality synthetic data. Experiments on 25 datasets show HS3F outperforms Forest Flow in quality, diversity, and speed. CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) is cited only in passing, as one of several prior GAN-based tabular generation methods listed in the related-work discussion, and is not run or benchmarked in the experiments.
preprint-generating-tabular-heterogeneou.needs: Affiliation-to-author mapping in the byline is ambiguous (superscript markers unclear); assignments of AIMS/Mila/SAIT to specific authors are best-effort inferences from layout, not certain from the text.

preprint-comprehensive-survey-generative.summary: This preprint surveys generative diffusion models applied to structured data, covering tabular and time series data across data-driven general tasks and domain-specific applications such as EHR generation, forecasting, biosignal enhancement, and recommendation systems. It reviews prior deep generative approaches (VAE, GAN) before diving into diffusion model theory and cataloguing dozens of diffusion-based methods across these domains. CTGAN is cited only once in passing as an example of GAN-based tabular data synthesis prior work, without being run or engaged with technically.

preprint-geometrically-aggregated-traini.summary: This preprint proposes geometrically-aggregated training samples (GATS), a privacy-preserving data-augmentation method that trains models on convex combinations of multiple patients' features instead of individual records, evaluated on CURIAL, eICU and UCI Adult datasets. GATS is benchmarked against state-of-the-art differentially private synthetic-data generators including MWEM, QUAIL, and PATE-CTGAN, and its performance is also compared to reported CTGAN accuracy figures from the literature. CTGAN (from the SDV family) is cited and described as the conditional tabular GAN backbone used inside the PATE-CTGAN baseline and as a literature comparison point, but is not itself run by the authors through the SDV library.
preprint-geometrically-aggregated-traini.needs: Unclear whether PATE-CTGAN, the actual baseline run, invokes the SDV-dev CTGAN implementation or an independent reimplementation; no library import or parameter evidence is given.

preprint-how-generative-models-improve-2.summary: This paper proposes a framework using generative deep learning models to synthesize satellite channel Line-of-Sight/Non-Line-of-Sight (LOS/NLOS) datasets for 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks, addressing data scarcity and privacy concerns in training ML-based LOS estimators. The authors train both CTGAN and TVAE on small real LOS traces to generate large synthetic datasets, comparing the two models on KS-test, Wasserstein distance, and KL divergence across satellite elevation angles, finding TVAE faster while both achieve comparable fidelity. CTGAN and TVAE, described by the authors as part of the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) package, are run directly as the two generative models whose outputs carry the entire empirical evaluation.
preprint-how-generative-models-improve-2.needs: Paper mislabels SDV as a 'TensorFlow' package (SDV/CTGAN is PyTorch-based); recorded as authors' own error, not corrected.

preprint-privacy-preserving-sharing-agri.summary: This paper proposes a framework for enforcing agricultural data-privacy-policy rules within a privacy-preserving synthetic data generation pipeline, extracting constraints from EU codes of conduct and GDPR to bound a generative model, then evaluating the synthetic agricultural data's downstream utility and resistance to re-identification and linkage attacks. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) appears only in the reference list as a cited work on synthesizing tabular data using GANs, with no SDV-family term found anywhere in the body text.

paper-resbit-categorical-2023.summary: Replaces one-hot encoding of categorical values with residual bit vectors, a hierarchical binary representation whose length grows logarithmically rather than linearly in cardinality, so that tables with high-cardinality columns stay tractable for generative models that would otherwise blow up in input dimension. CTGAN and TVAE are the first two of six baselines, named as the de facto standards for tabular generation, and the analysis reports CTGAN winning F1 on one dataset, failing on a highly imbalanced one, and both models losing sample diversity.

preprint-tabula-harnessing-language-mode.summary: This paper proposes Tabula, a tabular data synthesizer built on a large-language-model architecture that discards pretrained NLP weights and introduces token sequence compression and a customized padding strategy to cut training time while preserving synthetic data utility. It is evaluated against five state-of-the-art tabular synthesizers on six datasets for both ML utility and training-time efficiency. CTGAN is run as one of the baseline generators in these experiments, with its conditional vector and mode-specific preprocessing discussed as prior art that Tabula's LLM-based approach departs from.

paper-utility-disclosure-microdata-2022.summary: Puts synthetic data and conventional sampled microdata on the same risk-utility map, so that a data custodian can ask whether releasing a synthetic file is better or worse than releasing a sample, and applies the framework to four census microdata sets. CTGAN is one of the three synthesisers whose output is measured, pinned at version 0.4.3 and run five times per dataset under different random seeds; the paper also credits its mode-specific normalization for handling non-Gaussian and multimodal columns and varies the differential-privacy parameter across its runs.

preprint-fed-tda-federated-tabular-2022.summary: This paper proposes Fed-TDA, a federated tabular data augmentation method that synthesizes fake tables from simple pre-learned statistics (per-column distributions and global covariance) rather than training a generative model, aiming to address non-IID data and privacy concerns in federated learning. It demonstrates superior test performance, statistical similarity, and communication efficiency over federated GAN-based baselines on five real-world tabular datasets. CTGAN is cited only in passing as prior GAN-based work struggling with column distributions and correlations, with no SDV code run.

preprint-utility-recovery-incapability-n.summary: This paper audits the privacy-utility tradeoff of differentially private tabular data synthesizers, showing that DP-CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN fail to recover utility as privacy budgets are relaxed, while the Bayesian-network-based PrivBayes/DataSynthesizer does recover. The experiments run DP-CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN via the SmartNoise library across multiple UCI/Kaggle datasets and classifiers. CTGAN's original paper (Xu et al.) is cited only in a related-work list as the base architecture underlying DP-CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN, with no SDV-package code run.
preprint-utility-recovery-incapability-n.needs: CTGAN (Xu et al.) is cited as prior art in a related-work list; the actual synthesizers evaluated (DP-CTGAN, PATE-CTGAN) are third-party SmartNoise implementations built on CTGAN's architecture, not the sdv-dev package itself.

preprint-physiogan-training-high-fidelit.summary: PhysioGAN is a generative model combining an encoder, decoder, and discriminator to synthesize high-fidelity physiological sensor time-series data such as ECG and motion-sensor activity recognition signals, evaluated on classification accuracy, sample diversity, novelty, and imputation utility. In its introduction, the paper lists prior generative modeling work on tabular datasets, citing TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni, 2018) alongside other tabular GAN papers as examples of the tabular-data research direction it contrasts with its own focus on time-series sensor data. TGAN is only named in this brief related-work citation list and is never run or compared against experimentally.

paper-fed-tgan-2021.summary: Presents a federated learning framework for training tabular GANs across clients that cannot pool their data, addressing the fact that tabular generators need per-column global statistics before a common encoding can be agreed: it builds the categorical and continuous encoders at the federator without seeing local rows, and weights client model updates by a table-similarity score alongside row count, converging faster than multi-discriminator and vanilla federated baselines on non-IID and quantity-skewed splits. CTGAN is the generator being federated in every arm of the evaluation, and the privacy-preserving encoder construction is written against CTGAN's own scheme, one-hot for categoricals and variational Gaussian mixture mode-specific normalization for continuous columns, with CTGAN's default settings retained.

preprint-not-all-datasets-born-2020.summary: This preprint proposes a generic optimization framework for crafting adversarial examples on heterogeneous tabular datasets, embedding tabular inputs into a continuous latent space while preserving domain-specific validity constraints, and validates the approach on three real-world tabular datasets. OpenAlex metadata indicates the paper cites the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper, but no SDV-family term or CTGAN mention was found anywhere in the extracted full text or reference list, so the citation could not be located or confirmed in context.
preprint-not-all-datasets-born-2020.needs: Cannot verify the CTGAN citation in the actual text; the metadata-full text mismatch suggests either a missed reference-list entry or a mis-mapped citation by OpenAlex.

preprint-reinforcement-learning-multi-ag.summary: This preprint presents a data-driven approach combining a mathematical base algorithm with a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning system to optimize speed regulation on a metallurgical pickling line, addressing data scarcity via a two-step LSTM+CGAN synthetic data pipeline. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) appears only in the reference list among cited prior GAN-based tabular/sequential data synthesis works, with no evidence it was used in the actual pipeline.

repo-tabnetresearch.summary: A Russian-language bachelor's thesis investigating neural architectures for tabular data. Augmentation is done with the pre-1.0 `sdv.tabular` CTGAN and TVAE classes, scored with `sdv.evaluation`, and `sdv==0.14.0` is pinned. SDV supplies both the augmentation and the objective the thesis optimises against.
